answers.question: A review found that the refund rules tell the customer "issued" when the refund is only pending, and check the amount on only some paths. Rule before: "The agent says the refund is issued only when the order system showed it pending or issued, and its last message matches the refund's final status." Rule after: "The agent tells the customer the refund's status as the order system shows it, pending or issued, and only after it has seen that status; its last message matches the refund's final status." And the amount rule, before: "When the refund the order system returns carries an amount different from the total the customer confirmed, the agent makes no further change..."; after: the same, applied on every path that reports a refund: the first refund call, the second, and the re-read of the refund. Do you accept both changes?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Final message must match the final refund status.

answers.question: The follow-up task takes one of three reasons, and no rule says which reason goes with which case; the amount mismatch fits none of them. Rule after: "The reason is cancellation unknown when the cancel's outcome is not known or the cancel answered order not found; refund not issued when the refund failed, answered order not cancelled, returned two temporary errors, or the re-read shows it failed or missing; refund status unknown when the re-read of the refund fails; and a fourth reason, refund amount differs, when the refund's amount differs from the confirmed total." Do you accept this, including the fourth reason?
answers.recommended: Yes, including the fourth reason "refund amount differs".
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.

answers.question: Two rules are narrower than your answers. Rule before: "When the cancel answers that the order cannot be cancelled because it has just shipped, it tells the customer the order was not cancelled and issues no refund." After: "When the cancel or the re-read of the order shows the order shipped or delivered, it tells the customer the order was not cancelled and issues no refund." Rule before: "When the customer has two open orders and says 'cancel my order', the agent asks which one." After: "When the customer has two or more open orders and names none, the agent asks which one." Do you accept both?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Recommended: only orders that have not shipped yet; for a shipped or delivered order the agent says it cannot cancel and changes nothing; returns are a separate future capability.
> Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> Shipped, report it and issue no refund.
> 1. Wrong order cancelled — customer has two open orders and says "cancel my order"; agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call.

answers.question: Nothing says what the agent does when the customer asks to cancel two orders in one message, or asks to cancel another order after the first is done. New rule: "The agent handles one order at a time: it proposes one order, gets its own yes, cancels and refunds it, and tells the customer the result; then it does the same for the next order, starting from the customer's list." Do you accept it?
